title: Palm Beach Brownies

items.raw: 1 cup (225 g) unsalted butter, cut up
2 cups (225 g) walnuts, in large pieces

steps.text: Set it to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line a 9×13-inch pan with foil, pressing it into the corners, and butter the foil.
Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat or in the microwave, stirring until smooth. Set aside to cool slightly.

In a stand mixer, beat the eggs with the sugar, espresso, both extracts, and salt on high speed for 8 to 10 minutes, until very thick and pale. This long beating is what builds the famous crackly top.
On low speed, beat in the chocolate mixture just until combined, then the flour. Fold in half the walnuts by hand.

Spread in the pan, scatter the remaining walnuts over the top, and bake 33 to 38 minutes. The top will be crusty and cracked and a toothpick will come out with moist, fudgy crumbs. They are meant to be very soft inside; do not bake until dry.
Cool completely in the pan, then refrigerate overnight. Lift out by the foil, peel it away, and cut cold into 32 bars with a long, sharp knife.

notes.label: They are very rich
notes.text: cut them small. Thirty-two pieces from one pan is not stingy.

notes.label: High heat is deliberate
notes.text: the hot oven sets a crust on the outside while the center stays almost like fudge.

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: wrapped individually, they keep a week refrigerated and freeze beautifully. Many people prefer them straight from the freezer.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — I believe these are the famous Palm Beach Brownies from Maida Heatter’s dessert books: very rich, extra chocolate, espresso, walnuts, baked in a 9×13 pan and chilled before cutting. I have written my own version in that style. Can you confirm where yours comes from, and whose recipe it is in the family?
